source.toolchain: microsoft/vega-prover rev c0ee259, zk-cred-vega setup() (sirosfoundation/zk-cred-vega commit f86d71d)

notes: Closes the digestID interop gap fully: arbitrary spec-legal (<2^31) digestIDs at any of the 4 CBOR-uint widths (was hardcoded 0..3), via a new one-hot-cursor-chained splice primitive (onehot_cursor.rs/mso_splice.rs) that assembles the whole variable-length Sig_structure in a fixed-shape circuit. Also wires digest_id_extract into ClaimDigestStepCircuit so each claim's witnessed digestID is provably read from its own embedded bytes, cross-checked against the core circuit's witness by verify_and_check_binding (see binding_check_rejects_mismatched_digest_ids). Supersedes vega-mc-p256-v1-prover-key-r5 (deprecated). Still unpublished -- sha256_var/mso_splice/onehot_cursor are genuinely novel circuit code and have not had an independent security review yet, on top of the pre-existing ECDSA range-check gap. | deprecated: Superseded by r7: fixes a real under-constraint in digest_id_extract (high-order digestID value bits were unconstrained for CBOR length classes 0/1/2, letting a prover expose a fabricated digestID while the claim's bytes encoded another). See sirosfoundation/zk-cred-vega commit 246eee9 and its REVIEW-SCOPE.md P0-1.
